title: Ch 8 Test: Heredity
subject: Science
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Internal choice is given in some questions.
Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks. Section E: case-based, 4 marks.
Show crosses clearly with gametes and offspring wherever asked.

questions.q: Tall pea plants with violet flowers were crossed with short pea plants with white flowers. All the progeny had violet flowers, but almost half of them were short. The genetic make-up of the tall parent is:
questions.answer: (c) TtWW. Half the progeny are short, so the parent is Tt. All are violet, so the parent is WW.

questions.q: In human beings, the sex of the child is decided by:
questions.answer: (b) the father. The sperm carries either an X or a Y chromosome.

questions.q: In Mendel's monohybrid cross, the phenotypic ratio in the F_{2} generation is:
When a pure tall (TT) pea plant is crossed with a pure short (tt) plant, the F_{1} plants are:

**Assertion (A):** Human females have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes, both called X.
**Reason (R):** All children inherit an X chromosome from their mother.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.answer: (b). Both statements are true, but R is a consequence of A, not its explanation.

questions.q: What are dominant and recessive traits? Give one example of each from Mendel's experiments.
questions.answer: A dominant trait is expressed even when only one copy of its gene is present (e.g. tallness, T). A recessive trait is expressed only when both copies are of the recessive type (e.g. shortness, tt).

or.q: How do genes control traits? Explain with the example of plant height.
or.answer: A gene is a section of DNA that carries the information to make a protein, often an enzyme. Plant height depends on a growth hormone made with the help of an enzyme. If the gene makes an efficient enzyme, more hormone is made and the plant is tall. If the gene is altered and the enzyme is less efficient, less hormone is made and the plant is short.

questions.q: How is the sex of a child determined in human beings?
questions.answer: The mother has two X chromosomes, so every egg carries an X. The father has one X and one Y, so half the sperm carry X and half carry Y. If an X-carrying sperm fertilises the egg, the child is a girl (XX). If a Y-carrying sperm fertilises it, the child is a boy (XY).
marking: Mother XX gives X; father XY gives X or Y: 1

questions.q: Mendel crossed pea plants with round, yellow seeds (RRYY) with plants having wrinkled, green seeds (rryy).

subparts.q: What were the F_{1} seeds like?

subparts.answer: 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green

subparts.q: What does this cross show about the inheritance of the two traits?
subparts.answer: The two traits (seed shape and seed colour) are inherited independently of each other.

questions.q: Show, with gametes and a checkerboard, the result of crossing two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt × Tt). Give the phenotypic and genotypic ratios.
questions.answer: Gametes from each parent: T and t. Offspring: TT, Tt, Tt, tt. Phenotypic ratio: 3 tall : 1 short. Genotypic ratio: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt.

or.q: In a cross between pure tall (TT) and pure short (tt) pea plants, the short trait disappears in F_{1} but reappears in F_{2}. Explain why.
or.answer: All F_{1} plants are Tt. Tallness (T) is dominant, so it masks shortness and all F_{1} plants are tall. The gene for shortness is still present. When F_{1} plants are self-pollinated, one in four F_{2} plants gets two copies of t (tt) and is short. So the trait reappears.

subparts.q: Describe Mendel's experiment on plant height. Give the F_{1} and F_{2} results.
subparts.answer: Mendel crossed pure tall (TT) with pure short (tt) pea plants. All F_{1} plants were tall (Tt), with no medium-height plants. When the F_{1} plants were self-pollinated, the F_{2} generation had tall and short plants in the ratio 3 : 1 (genotypes TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1).

subparts.q: Give two reasons why the garden pea was a good choice for Mendel's experiments.
subparts.answer: (Any two) It has many clear contrasting visible traits (tall/short, round/wrinkled seeds, violet/white flowers). It has a short life cycle. It normally self-pollinates but can easily be cross-pollinated. It produces many seeds.

or.q:
(a) What is variation? Why is it important for a species? [2]
(b) Explain sex determination in humans with the help of a cross. [3]
or.answer: (a) Variation means the differences among individuals of a species. It is important because some variants may survive better if the environment changes, which helps the species survive. (b) Mother (XX) × Father (XY). Gametes: egg X; sperm X or Y. Offspring: XX (girl) and XY (boy) in a 1 : 1 ratio. So the sex of the child depends on which sperm fertilises the egg.

sections.title: Section E
sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: A student crossed pea plants with violet flowers (VV) with plants having white flowers (vv). All F_{1} plants had violet flowers. When the F_{1} plants were self-pollinated, out of 400 F_{2} plants, about 300 had violet flowers and 100 had white flowers.

subparts.q: Write the genotype of the F_{1} plants.
Out of the 300 violet-flowered F_{2} plants, how many are expected to be pure-breeding (VV)? Explain.
subparts.answer: The F_{2} genotypes are VV : Vv : vv = 1 : 2 : 1, so out of 400 plants we expect 100 VV, 200 Vv and 100 vv. So about 100 of the 300 violet plants are VV.
